findings: What sets the damp schools apart lies in the bed above it -> What sets the damp schools apart lies in the bed above that base (q3 rationale, C rebuttal, third sentence - the whole paragraph is new at fleet-repair-3). The pronoun has to reach back over two nearer singulars, “a bed” and “the day”, in the clause immediately before it, and the nearest of them, a bed, makes “the bed above it” nonsense. NEW DEFECT, fleet-repair-3.

so the hoof reaches it after all. -> so the load of those hoofprints reaches it after all. (q2 rationale, C rebuttal, final clause; written at fleet-repair-1 and untouched since). The passage supports compaction transmitted through the bed, not penetration: the layer in question sits 50-130 mm down and the unit teaches three sentences earlier that a cold hoof “breaks the surface”. As written the limb teaches a learner that a hoof reaches 130 mm, which the unit's own physics denies.
justification: Read aloud in full: title, five paragraphs of passage, five prompts, twenty options, five rationales, with two sentences taken either side of both fleet-repair-3 spans. THE r3 PRESCRIPTION THAT WAS WRITTEN LANDED AND READS BETTER THAN THE FRAME IT REPLACED: “The other arenas are a mixed set – “some of them older than this one” – and the waxed floors swing whatever age they are.” The appositive takes the fragment cleanly where “include” could not, the spaced en dashes are the unit's existing system, and not a character inside the quotation moved. THE PRESCRIPTION THAT WAS NOT WRITTEN: my r1 finding “it holds its state” was discharged by deleting the option that carried it. On the read-aloud test alone that is the better outcome - a collocation repair inside a clause that a second gate wanted gone would have been wasted work - but the replacement clause the round wrote in its place is not defect-free, and that is the first finding above. Second checked span of the new option: “A membrane under them holds the water in, so the bed does not dry through the day.” Read aloud this is sound English - hold in is the ordinary verb for an impermeable barrier and intransitive dry takes a durative adverbial without strain; “them” and “the water” both resolve out of the stem. It is the option's SHAPE that fails, and that is vote 3's finding, not mine. Re-cleared on this round's read, each with its reason: “the pan” in paragraph 5 is an unglossed first-mention definite but is standing agricultural usage and no item turns on it; the q1 key's “opposite arithmetic directions” still does not collide with the passage's “they moved together”, because the passage's colon expands together as in-concert and the two texts are never adjacent on the page; “though not in the way the yard had blamed it” is compressed but a recognised elliptical frame. Bare definites swept across the whole passage: school, tractor, leveller, floor, membrane, yard, boot, collar, gate, grid, wax, bed, tines, pan – every one is either introduced or frame-recoverable inside its own sentence.

findings: The floor that swings is itself “laid over a membrane and crushed stone”, so a base of that kind cannot be what keeps a bed steady through the day. -> What keeps those beds damp is named in the stem and in the passage alike – they are “kept damp with a sprinkler” – so the water in them is put there from above and wants nothing under the bed to hold it. (q3 rationale, C rebuttal, second sentence, new at fleet-repair-3.) Two failures in one sentence: the limb rebuts a STEADINESS claim while the option it faces makes a DRYING claim, and the inference does not go through, because the floor it cites is waxed and unsprinkled, so its membrane has no water to hold and its behaviour shows nothing about a membrane under a watered bed. The passage's own answer to C - the sprinkler, which is in the stem - is never brought against it. NEW DEFECT, fleet-repair-3.

A school that is kept warm will ride in February much as it rides in July. -> A school that is heated in winter will stop riding deep on a July afternoon. (q5 option B; written at generation and never edited in any round.) As it stands B is TRUE on the unit's own mechanism: the key teaches that how the floor rides turns on the room's temperature, so a room held at one temperature rides the same in both months. Its rebuttal answers a different claim - that warmth is a cure - and so teaches past the option. The replacement is false in the direction the existing rebuttal already kills. This moves an option text and owes a G-KEY / G-DISTRACTOR re-clear.

The damp schools differ from this one in a single respect the passage keeps in view: there is no wax on their sand. -> The passage names the damp schools by two things at once, and the one Pallenmoor's comparison turns on is the coating: there is no wax on their sand. (q3 rationale, key paragraph, first sentence; fleet-repair-1 text, untouched since.) The passage sentence the paragraph later leans on names two differences in one breath, “laid on plain sand and fibre” AND “kept damp with a sprinkler”, and the sprinkler is the property the stem itself picks the class out by. A single respect is contradicted inside the paragraph that asserts it.
justification: Class-by-class sweep. MISQUOTATION, mechanical and not by eye: every span between U+201C and U+201D in all five rationales extracted by regex and tested with `span in passage` against the shipped passage string – 31 spans, 31 literal members, 0 near-misses, 0 failures, on this round's bytes. The count is unchanged from r2 and r3 because fleet-repair-3 moved no character inside any quotation mark; I re-ran rather than inherited, since the round rewrote two paragraphs of q3. DIAGNOSIS CURRENCY, option by option, twenty of them: nineteen limbs describe the option they now face. The twentieth is q3 C and it is the first finding above – the option asserts that the bed does not dry, the limb rebuts a claim about the bed staying steady. DIRECTION AUDIT: q1 C down/up and harder-in-cold correct; q1 D correctly inverts the seasons-versus-arenas comparison; q2 A correctly puts the better wax at the bottom; q2 D's fibre split correct; q3 D correctly refuses the timing artefact; q4 A, B, C and D all correct and the r2 repair of “what he does claim” still stands; q5 A correctly separates a stiffened coating at three degrees from ice; q5 C and q5 D preserve the temperature-over-tractor ranking. INTERNAL CONTRADICTION: two found, both above – the single-respect assertion in the q3 key paragraph, and the steadiness/drying swap in the q3 C limb. The q5 B limb is a third failure of a different kind: not self-contradictory, but valid reasoning aimed at a proposition the option does not contain. Countability, articles, tense and aspect, NPIs, relatives and mixed comparisons: clean. Of my three findings exactly one is new this round; the other two are copy no repair round has ever opened.

findings: A membrane under them holds the water in, so the bed does not dry through the day. -> A membrane under them holds the water in and keeps the bed from drying through the day. (q3 option C, written at fleet-repair-3.) FORM TELL, and it is the round's own making. The comma-plus-so consequence shape occurs in exactly one option set in this unit, q3, and fleet-repair-3 raised its incidence there from two of four to three of four: A “They went down more recently, so their sand has not had nine years of hooves on it.”, C as rebuilt, D “They are read at a different hour, so the change falls between his two grids.” The key, B, is now the ONLY option in the set without it, so odd-one-out-on-form selects the key. The option it replaced used “, and”, which is why the tell did not exist before this round. The replacement is 17 words against the current 17, so the set stays A 17 / B 16 / C 17 / D 15, ratio 1.13, key not longest; it carries no absolutizer, so the unit-wide count stays at 1; and it keeps C off the wax-presence variable, which is what the round was buying. NEW DEFECT, fleet-repair-3.

A 40-token AmE regex (color/fiber/meter/center/-ize/-ization/analyze/leveling/aging/artifact/percent/gotten/toward/gray/spoiled/defense/tire/trunk/railroad/neighbor and the rest) over all five layers: zero hits in every layer. TYPOGRAPHY PER LAYER, recounted: title nothing; passage U+2019 4, U+2013 4, U+201C/U+201D 2/2; prompts U+2019 1; options U+2019 4; rationales U+2019 7, U+2013 4, U+201C/U+201D 31/31. QUOTE-TERMINAL PUNCTUATION, re-derived non-circularly over all 55 spans in the four units: a stop stands inside iff the span begins at a passage sentence boundary AND the passage terminates it with a stop at exactly that point AND the citation is colon-introduced. 6 spans take the stop inside, 49 outside, 0 mismatches. findings: A settlement is what closes a dispute, which is the far end of the process from the stage being described. -> A settlement is what closes a dispute, and closing is the far end of the process from the stage being described. (gap-3 rationale.) The relative takes the wrong antecedent on the read: the nearest candidate is “a dispute”, and a dispute is not the far end of a process. The intended head is “what closes a dispute”, two constituents back. fleet-repair-2 edited the tail of this clause (“the one” -> “the stage”) and left the relative untouched, so the defect is generation-era and has now survived three rounds.

a response to a request is the one thing an instinct cannot be -> a room that has been asked is doing what it was asked, not what it could not help (gap-5 rationale, closing clause of the Instinctively limb, generation-era). The aphorism is false as stated – instinctive responses to requests are ordinary, a startle at a shouted warning among them – and the learner is being taught a categorical rule in order to reach a conclusion that only needs the prompted/spontaneous distinction. The replacement carries the real ground.
justification: Read aloud: passage, five prompts, twenty single-word options and five rationales, two sentences either side of every fleet-repair-2 span. NOTHING IN THIS UNIT MOVED AT ROUND 3. It is the one unit of the four with no fleet-repair-3 entry at all, and its repair log sits at $.generator_meta.repair_log rather than $.repair_log, a schema divergence from its three siblings that is worth a coordinator's eye even though it is not a language defect. I did not take the absent entry as evidence: I tested every student-facing string round 3 quoted for this unit against the current bytes and every one is present verbatim once the verdict's own ellipses and filled cloze gaps are discounted. Both r3 findings therefore still read as discharged – “the far end of the process from the stage being described” and “a room clapping out of keenness”. The two fleet-repair-2 passage sentences still read as native BrE essay prose and “one” in “every hall has one” still resolves harmlessly on either antecedent. My two findings are both in the rationale layer and both predate every repair round. Checked and cleared with reasons: the half-second of paragraph 1 and the fifth of a second of paragraph 2 are not in conflict, since a 0.2 s settling time sits inside a 0.5 s onset window and the passage asserts no identity between them; “who were slow” is a past relative inside a gnomic present but marks anteriority within the single event being narrated and reads correctly; “the recorder” and “the summer concert” are frame-definites a school-hall opening licenses; “how long is decent” follows the attested how-much-is-enough pattern and needs no expletive; “it is not permitted to run long” is transatlantic register, not an AmE marker. The unit contains no apostrophe in any layer and no sentence suffers for it.

findings: Only a word for warmth supplies that tension: a hall that gives a child something wholehearted and then stops it after five seconds really is doing two things at once. -> Of the four, only a word for warmth both supplies that tension and can be said of a noise: a hall that gives a child something wholehearted and then stops it after five seconds really is doing two things at once. (gap-4 rationale, key paragraph.) INTERNAL CONTRADICTION: the paragraph asserts that warmth alone supplies the concessive tension, then three sentences later concedes that Outspoken “is a real adjective at the forceful end” and disqualifies it on what it may be predicated of, not on tension. Both cannot be true; the replacement states the two criteria the paragraph actually applies.
justification: Class-by-class sweep plus the cloze-specific checks. MISQUOTATION, mechanical: all 9 curly-quoted spans across the five rationales extracted by regex and tested with `span in passage` – 9 of 9 literal members, 0 failures, on this round's bytes. RATIONALE/OPTION CORRESPONDENCE, gap by gap, against the option strings in the file now: gap 1 names Hence, Rather and Elsewhere; gap 2 names fall, break and cut; gap 3 names transaction, bargain and settlement; gap 4 names Brief, Rehearsed and Outspoken; gap 5 names Eagerly, Instinctively and Narrowly. Every distractor in every set is diagnosed and no limb names a word that is not in its set. POS-UNIFORMITY holds gap by gap (sentence adverbs; bare verbs after may not, each forming a real phrasal verb with in; singular abstract nouns; adjectives; -ly manner adverbs), so sense alone discriminates, which is what the design requires and what the rationales claim. SINGLE IDIOMATIC WORD per gap confirmed; each near-miss is closed on a stated ground. INTERNAL CONTRADICTION: one found, the finding above. Cleared after a second look: “a third count” in the gap-4 Outspoken limb mis-numbers slightly, since Rehearsed is said to fail on two counts of its own, but it reads as a third KIND of ground and misleads nobody; the gap-5 exclusion of Eagerly rests on a pragmatic rather than a literal entailment, and holds, because “not the same sound” idiomatically means not as good in this frame. Diagnosis currency is exact throughout: no option in this unit has moved since fleet-repair-1 and every limb still faces the word it was written for.

Variety and typography per layer, swept mechanically. SPELLING VARIETY: declared BrE and carried where it can be – passage realise, organises, plus BrE lexis school hall, a leaving do, the second row; rationales organise/organises, realise, queue, unsignalled with the doubled l. The twenty options are single common words and none of them is variety-discriminating, which is structural and not a defect (fall here is the phrasal verb, not the season, so it is not an AmE marker). A 40-token AmE regex over all five layers: zero hits. TYPOGRAPHY PER LAYER: title nothing; passage U+2013 1, the byline dash, and nothing else; prompts nothing; options nothing; rationales U+2013 6, U+201C/U+201D 9/9. U+2019 zero in EVERY layer – the unit genuinely contains no apostrophe, so passage and rationale cannot diverge on apostrophe style – and U+2014, U+0022, U+0027 and U+2026 are all zero. Curly pairs balanced. One system, and the same system the other three units use. QUOTE-TERMINAL PUNCTUATION: this unit contributes 9 of the batch's 55 spans and none of them takes a stop inside. Under the re-derived rule that is correct: none is a complete passage sentence terminated at exactly its own end, and the one terminal-looking span, “it is not the same sound the recorder player got”, is a mid-sentence fragment. The rule predicts all 9. LENGTH TELLS: impossible in a single-word cloze set, and confirmed – every option in every gap is one word. COPULAR EPIGRAMS, script-derived: 12 nominal or adjectival copular main clauses plus 2 existential, 14 in all, over 18 passage sentences. At 0.67 copular clauses per sentence this is twice the density of elf-b22-001 (0.34) and six times elf-b22-004 (0.10), and it is the highest in the batch by a distance. I record it as a measurement and not a defect: the essay lane licenses the aphoristic cadence, the gap sentences themselves account for three of the twelve, and no sentence reads as padding. Note on method, since round 3 reported 5/6/3/1 for the four units: those figures do not re-derive from any stated rule and are a judgement subset of the mechanical count. Mine is reproducible – finite BE as main verb, not followed by a participle, predicate nominal or adjectival, existential and bare-locative predicates counted separately – and only elf-b22-004 agrees between the two methods, at 1.

findings: and hangs the wrong conclusion on it, since urgent work is what a hospital would want a tube for. -> and hangs the wrong conclusion on it, a conclusion that tempts because urgent work is exactly what a hospital would want a tube for. (Option C paragraph, second clause; generation-era, untouched by fleet-repair-1, -2 or -3.) Read aloud, the “since” attaches as the ground for the assertion in front of it, and the assertion in front of it is that the conclusion is WRONG. The sentence therefore states that C is wrong because a hospital would want a tube for urgent work, which is the opposite of the intended teaching: that is the reason C TEMPTS. The replacement moves the clause onto the right host.
justification: Read aloud: title, four short paragraphs and a one-line coda, one prompt, four options and the single rationale with its five paragraphs, two sentences either side of every fleet-repair-2 span. FLEET-REPAIR-3 TOUCHED NO STUDENT-FACING BYTE HERE AND I VERIFIED THAT RATHER THAN TAKING IT: the round records student_facing_sha256_before = student_facing_sha256_after = 2ac1b1bff777b108e4329c764a831a58bf247c5062717edcb6b2b42b939ea10c under a stated recipe (sha256 over json.dumps of title, passage and questions, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2). I recomputed that digest from the file on disk and it reproduces character for character, so the shipped student-facing layer is the layer round 3 measured, and the round's two edits really were confined to $.generator_meta.rule8_sibling_sweep and $.repair_log[2]. The r2 coda “Nobody has lined the other bins.” still reads as the better close: present perfect, unforced negative subject, “the other bins” taking its antecedent straight from “Two bins are lined with foam”, and the piece ends on the size of what is undone. The passage still reads as native BrE hospital reportage throughout. Checked and cleared, each with its reason: “the packed cells”, “the ward”, “the loop” and “the patient’s” are all first-mention definites, and all four are standard frame-definites of hospital-laboratory register that a native reads without a stumble – there is no patient anywhere in the passage and none is needed; “what the instrument gave back” is an unusual verb for an instrument but vivid rather than wrong; “with the one event worth naming falling at the journey’s end” is a fair inference and not an over-reading, because “Between stations” only means anything if the trace also covers the stations; “a porter walks those down” is metonymy for the samples and is ordinary usage.

Class-by-class sweep. MISQUOTATION, mechanical: all 7 curly-quoted spans in the single rationale extracted by regex and tested with `span in passage` – 7 of 7 literal members, 0 failures, on this round's bytes. LETTER INTEGRITY AFTER THE r2 RELETTERING, re-run and not inherited, because it is this unit's live risk: the key paragraph argues the accelerometer and the stop at the far end and A is “The harm is done at the moment a carrier reaches the far end.”; the second paragraph argues colour and ward and B is the ward-colour option; the third argues blood gases and C is the blood-gases option; the fourth argues loop speed and D is the slowed-loop option. $.questions[0].key is A. No paragraph names a letter it no longer owns, and the paragraphs run in letter order with the mechanism coda last. DIRECTION AUDIT: the coda has the cells bursting first and the potassium passing into the plasma after, so the reported figure is too HIGH and the pink is haemoglobin released rather than present beforehand – the one direction in this unit that inverts easily, and it is stated correctly and explicitly. The B limb correctly denies the ward the colour; the C limb correctly reverses the route; the D limb correctly refuses the slowing on “The loop runs at the speed it always has.” INTERNAL CONTRADICTION: none. DIAGNOSIS CURRENCY: all four options are diagnosed as they now stand. The one thing I considered and did not raise as a correspondence defect: the C limb imports a clinical fact the passage never states (that blood gases cannot be left standing) in order to grant the option its premise, but the kill itself lands on a citable span, so the teaching does not depend on the import. My one finding for this unit is a connective failure inside the C paragraph and belongs to vote 1.

Variety and typography per layer. SPELLING VARIETY: declared BrE and carried in the student-facing layers, not only the rationale – passage colour, haemoglobin, plus BrE lexis senior biomedical scientist, round the loop, porter, the ward; options colour, spoilt; rationale colour, haemoglobin. A 40-token AmE regex (color/hemoglobin/spoiled/analyze/-ize/-ization/center/fiber/meter/percent/railroad/neighbor and the rest) over all five layers: zero hits in every layer. TYPOGRAPHY PER LAYER: title nothing; passage U+2019 4, U+2013 1 (the byline), U+201C/U+201D 3/3; prompt nothing; options nothing; rationale U+2019 2, U+2013 0, U+201C/U+201D 7/7. U+2014 zero, U+0022 zero, U+0027 zero, U+2026 zero; curly pairs balanced; one system. QUOTE-TERMINAL PUNCTUATION: this unit supplies three of the batch's six inside-stop spans, more than any other, and all three are correct under the re-derived rule – “Nothing shows on the ward; the colour comes with the spinning.”, “Blood gases have never gone by tube; a porter walks those down.” and “The loop runs at the speed it always has.”, each a complete passage sentence terminated at exactly that point and each colon-introduced. Its two visible counter-cases still behave: “It’s the stop at the far end that does it” takes the stop outside because the passage punctuates it with a comma before she says, and “rejects are down by about half” because the span is a coordinate clause and not a sentence. The cross-unit call this unit argued for in round 2 has held for a second round: I re-derived the rule non-circularly over all 55 spans in the four units and it predicts every placement, 0 mismatches, in both directions. LENGTH TELL: the key is joint-shortest at 13 words against 14/13/12, ratio 1.17. COPULAR EPIGRAMS, script-derived: 4 nominal or adjectival copular main clauses plus 2 locative, 6 in all, over 13 passage sentences (0.31 per sentence), the second-lowest density in the batch and right for reportage; the r2 coda is non-copular and did not raise it.

findings: the claim is of “November 1845” -> the claim is dated “November 1845” (rationale, C paragraph, second sentence; fleet-repair-1 text, untouched since). The clause sits in a two-part parallel whose first half is “The pegging is dated “The previous October””, and the switch from is dated to is of breaks the parallel and reads as a stumble: English dates a claim, it does not say a claim is OF a month. The replacement restores the parallel and changes nothing inside the quotation marks.
justification: Read aloud: title, the ten-sentence passage, the prompt, four options and the two-paragraph rationale, two sentences either side of every fleet-repair-2 span. FLEET-REPAIR-3 TOUCHED NO STUDENT-FACING BYTE HERE AND I VERIFIED THAT RATHER THAN TAKING IT: the round records a combined digest 6fd79437a1127db3536035b8b9042881975664ccc211d0e77fcdf2e019fd97d4 before and after, under a stated recipe (sha256 over json.dumps of title, passage and a trimmed questions array, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, compact separators), plus six per-layer digests. I recomputed the combined digest and all six per-layer digests from the file on disk and every one reproduces, so the shipped student-facing layer is the layer round 3 read and the round's eight edits really were confined to generator_meta. The r2 rebuild of option A still reads as clean English on one pass and “Ruddiforth’s neighbour” is established by “between two Huntingdonshire farms”; the r2 it-cleft “so it was the neighbour’s side that brought the railway into the letters” still puts the correction where a learner meets it. The passage is period-accurate throughout and the archival present of “The letters run to March; both sides agree” still sits beside the narrative past without jarring. Checked and cleared: “the railway company” is a first-mention definite with no prior railway anywhere in the passage, and it is the most exposed bare definite in the batch, but in an 1845 deposited-plan frame it is recoverable at once to a native reader, the option and the rationale both use the same definite, and repairing it in the passage would break a quoted span, so it stays; “the hedge”, “the stone gap”, “the lane” and “The letters” are in-medias-res definites of the period-essay register and each is defined by the sentence after it; “and had stood since the enclosure” coordinates correctly with “was a thorn bank” across the participials; the A limb's two its resolve without a re-read.

findings: the bank was “cut from above by one and cleaned from below by the other, and had stood since the enclosure” -> the bank was “cut from above by one and cleaned from below by the other”, and it “had stood since the enclosure” (rationale, B paragraph). HOST FRAME WILL NOT TAKE THE QUOTED SPAN, the same structural class round 3 found in elf-b22-001's q3 A rebuttal and the identical failure mode: the host copula was governs the whole quotation, so the second conjunct reads “the bank was ... had stood since the enclosure”, which is ill-formed. In the passage that conjunct hangs off “It was a thorn bank” and needs its own subject when it is lifted out. Splitting the quotation supplies one; both halves remain byte-identical passage members and neither is terminal, so the punctuation rule is untouched. fleet-repair-1 text; fleet-repair-2 edited the frame AROUND it (“the second sentence removes it” -> “two sentences remove it”) and left the defect standing; round 3 did not see it.

A is a true detail with the two sides exchanged, and it survives a hurried reading because the tracing really is in the file; -> A takes the one thing the file records and denies it of the side that did it, and it survives a hurried reading because the tracing really is in the file; (rationale, A paragraph, opening). DIAGNOSIS CURRENCY: the gloss was written at fleet-repair-1 for the fleet-repair-1 option A, “Ruddiforth’s attorney put the railway plan into the letters to strengthen his client’s claim.”, for which two sides exchanged was exactly right. fleet-repair-2 rebuilt A into a NEGATION, “Ruddiforth’s neighbour answered the claim without bringing the railway company’s plan into the letters.”, and did not touch the gloss. A negation contains no detail that can be true and exchanges nothing, so a learner sent to find the exchanged detail in A will not find one. The limb's closing clause, added at r2, already corrects in the right direction; only the opening is stale. DEFECT INTRODUCED AT fleet-repair-2, surviving round 3.
justification: Class-by-class sweep. MISQUOTATION, mechanical: all 8 curly-quoted spans in the rationale extracted by regex and tested with `span in passage` – 8 of 8 literal members, 0 failures, on this round's bytes. Membership is not the problem in this unit; HOST GRAMMAR is, and that is the first finding above – a span can be a perfect member and still be ungrammatical where it is spliced, which is precisely the defect class round 3 opened in the arena unit and did not then look for here. The two landmark spans the key turns on, “from the stone gap down to the lane” and “along the bank, from the ash to the culvert”, match character for character, as does the bridging sentence. ARITHMETIC AND CHRONOLOGY: 1839 to November 1845 is six years, as the B limb says; the C limb keeps telling-order and event-order apart correctly, with the pegging of “The previous October” before the claim of November 1845; “it makes no claim about compensation, which never fell due” reconciles with “no land was taken”. ATTRIBUTION: the passage has the neighbour's attorney enclosing the tracing and the A limb's closing clause names the right side, so the KILL is correct even though the GLOSS in front of it is stale. RATIONALE/OPTION CORRESPONDENCE, all four: D, B and C are diagnosed as they stand; A is not, and that is the second finding. INTERNAL CONTRADICTION: none. Both findings are pre-existing; fleet-repair-3 introduced nothing here, which the per-layer digests corroborate and which I confirmed by recomputing them.

Variety and typography per layer. SPELLING VARIETY: declared BrE and carried by every layer that can carry it – passage neighbour, autumn, railway against AmE railroad, plus period-BrE lexis the enclosure, attorney, deposited plan, thorn laid, timber, culvert; prompt neighbouring; options neighbour, railway; rationale neighbour, railway, attorney/attorneys. A 40-token AmE regex (neighbor/railroad/fall-for-autumn/color/center/-ize/-ization/percent/toward and the rest) across all five layers: zero hits. TYPOGRAPHY PER LAYER: title nothing; passage U+2019 3, U+2013 1 (the byline); prompt nothing; options U+2019 2; rationale U+2019 5, U+2013 0, U+201C/U+201D 8/8. U+2014 zero, U+0022 zero, U+0027 zero, U+2026 zero; curly pairs balanced; one system, and the same one the batch uses. QUOTE-TERMINAL PUNCTUATION: this unit has one inside-stop span, “An ash grew in the stone gap; a culvert ran under the lane.”, colon-introduced and a complete passage sentence terminated at exactly that point, and it is correct under the re-derived rule. Its useful counter-case still behaves: “The neighbour’s attorney enclosed a tracing of the railway company’s deposited plan” IS a complete passage sentence but is not colon-introduced – it is spliced as a predicate complement and the host continues with a comma – so it correctly takes no stop inside.
